name: fixlane-security
description: Check the developer software on your machine against known security incidents and get reviewed fix procedures, from the public Fixlane server.

interface.longDescription: Fixlane checks the developer software on your computer against known, reviewed security incidents. Ask whether a program such as Chrome, Node.js or VS Code is safe, or let the assistant list what is installed (names and versions only) and compare it with the versions that fix each incident. For every affected program Fixlane returns a reviewed fix procedure: a read-only check first, then the update, which the assistant shows you and runs only after you agree. Phones get manual steps only. The data is public and read-only, no account is needed and nothing you ask is stored. Fixlane covers actively exploited vulnerabilities and malicious packages in developer tools; it is not a general antivirus and does not cover every program.
defaultPrompt: Is my computer safe? Check my installed developer software.
Is my version of Chrome affected by a known security issue?
What are the newest security incidents for macOS?

positive.prompt: Is Google Chrome on my Linux machine affected by any known security issue?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Chrome incidents with severity, "exploited in the wild", fixed version and incident id, and offers the fix procedure.

positive.prompt: Show me the fix procedure for Fixlane incident 2010 on Linux.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the danger, the fixed version and the procedure (read-only detection first, then the fix) and asks before changing anything.

positive.prompt: What are the three newest security incidents for macOS?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists three incidents, newest first, with severity and date.

positive.prompt: Give me one fix prompt for everything I should update now on Linux.
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes the digest (components, critical, exploited) and shows the digest procedure; asks before running it.

positive.prompt: My Linux machine has Google Chrome 140.0.7339.0 and Node.js (I do not know the version). Which of them have known issues?
positive.expected_behavior: Chrome is affected (incident id and fixed version are shown); Node.js is unknown because no version was given, not "safe"; offers the fix procedure for Chrome.

negative.description: Not a software question: the tool says it is not a program name; the assistant gives no hacking help and asks for a program or package name instead.
negative.prompt: How do I read my neighbour's wifi password?

negative.description: Unknown incident: the tool says the incident is not served; the assistant invents no procedure and offers the newest incidents instead.
negative.prompt: Show me the fix procedure for Fixlane incident 999999999 on Linux.

negative.description: Digest for a phone: there is no digest for phones; the assistant offers the newest iOS incidents (manual steps only) and runs nothing.
negative.prompt: Give me the Fixlane digest for my iPhone.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: five read-only tools, one skill.
